source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To delete privilege mapping, use the following command:
1.openbmctool.py <connection options> ldap privilege-mapper delete --groupName=<groupName>

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: openbmctool.py (from openbmc-tools, pip/install) + BMC + LDAP group name
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Delete privilege mapping (delete privilege mapping): openbmctool.py ${BMC_CONN:?operator must supply openbmctool target, e.g. http://${BMC_USER}:${BMC_PASS}@${BMC_IP}:8080/} ldap privilege-mapper delete --groupName=${LDAP_GROUP:?operator must supply the LDAP group name (DN or CN)} (openbmctool from openbmc-tools, user installs + supplies the LDAP group/privilege values). Agent runs the tool and captures its output; create/delete changes BMC auth config so user confirms.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the openbmctool command output/HTTP status so the user confirms the mapping was deleted (200 OK).
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: changing LDAP privilege mapping affects BMC auth; use the intended group/privilege and restore if needed.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires exact mapping/group identity, complete inventory, pinned method, one approved delete, affected/control/local authorization tests, independent recovery and optional explicit restore.

original_test_intent: Verify openbmctool deletes exactly one approved LDAP group-to-BMC privilege mapping, removes the expected effective authorization for affected users and leaves unrelated mappings, local administration and recovery access intact.
original_method: Pin openbmctool, inventory every mapping and correlate the canonical group identity, role, directory members and sessions; select a unique noncritical mapping and preserve a restore definition; verify local recovery; delete it once after approval; read back the complete inventory; test affected, unrelated/control and local users; restore only if explicitly required.
manual_activity: An access-control owner identifies the exact unique mapping, confirms it is safe to remove, defines affected/control/local-user expectations and authorizes restore scope. A human retains independent recovery and observes authorization impact. Automation may delete one approved mapping and collect redacted readback but may not infer the group from a partial name or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware and pinned supported openbmctool/API version
Canonical group DN/CN, realm, case, nesting and unique mapping identity
Current mapped role, affected membership and active-session facts
Complete mapping/account/role baseline and unrelated mappings to preserve
Exact mapping backup/restore operation and approval
safety_requirements: Do not delete using an ambiguous short group name, multiple-match identity, only administrator/recovery mapping or production-wide group.
Do not expose credentials in URLs, command lines, history, processes, logs, screenshots or review JSON; do not clear audit logs or delete the directory group itself.
Compare the complete mapping inventory and directory membership before the write, including role and active sessions, and prove independent local recovery.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one exact delete. Do not bulk-delete, alter another mapping, terminate unrelated sessions, retry or restore without approval.
Do not accept HTTP success as deletion or access proof; read back the whole inventory and test affected/control/local authorization non-destructively.
Stop on wrong/multiple target, unexpected access loss, unchanged mapping, unrelated-map change, recovery failure or ambiguous session behavior; use approved local recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/tool, canonical group/mapping uniqueness, baseline, role/session impact, authorization matrix, recovery and restore; present one delete for approval.
After approval, delete only the exact mapping with protected authentication and capture redacted response/audit plus complete post-inventory.
Test affected, unrelated/control and local-admin authorization from independent sessions and compare all mappings to baseline.
Restore only if explicitly approved, archive evidence and stop without directory-group deletion, bulk change, retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve canonical mapping identity, delete scope, affected/control authorization results and session expectations.
Approve the pinned one-mapping delete, independent recovery and any exact restore.
Review inventory, authorization, audit and recovery evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The delete verb matches the source, but the provided groupName may not be unique, BMC_CONN can expose credentials and HTTP status does not prove the relation is gone or the right access changed. The extra reference to group/privilege values does not define the target's current role.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact pinned openbmctool `ldap privilege-mapper delete` once only after resolving groupName to one persisted mapping and securing authentication; verify full state and authorization separately.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The openbmctool delete command, groupName input, successful-command Criterion, no Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review adds selection and evidence without modifying Master.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve one safe mapping unambiguously, delete it once, reconcile the full inventory and prove affected-versus-control/local authorization before any optional restore.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected OpenBMC LDAP privilege-mapper and approved test directory realm.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/API, openbmctool commit/runtime and directory server version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Pinned openbmc-tools privilege-mapper schema, vendor BMC role/session model and Project access-control/recovery policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds unique identity, role/session impact, effective authorization, unrelated-map preservation and recovery while retaining the source delete action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A vendor API override does not prove openbmctool; absence from one response does not prove effective access change; directory-group deletion is outside scope.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Unique mapping, complete inventory, affected/control users, recovery and restore.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-group deletion can remove broad/admin access; sessions may retain authorization until reauthentication; restoring by guess can create duplicate or elevated mappings.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor API or WebUI only when it records the original openbmctool method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, exact mapping/state/auth equivalence and unverified tool coverage. Read-only listing cannot replace the functional delete.
expected_evidence: Approved BMC/firmware/tool, canonical group/mapping/role/member/session identity, full redacted mapping baseline and independent recovery proof
One protected delete response and audit event tied to the exact mapping with no secret exposure
Complete post-delete inventory proving only the target relation changed
Affected-user denial or reduced role, unrelated/control-user continuity, local-admin continuity and defined session behavior
Optional approved exact restore or final-state record, no directory-group/bulk deletion or retry and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request deletion of one privilege mapping by groupName and successful command submission. Exact group identity and expected access/session effects are Project readiness inputs, not competing source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The one-mapping deletion objective is identifiable. A complete inventory, canonical group and recovery plan can make the action safe, so missing inputs make execution pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but removes credential-bearing shorthand and HTTP-only proof, adds unique target, full inventory, effective authorization and recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its critical controls and emphasizes active-session semantics and complete before/after reconciliation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic command-success evidence with exact relation, authorization-boundary and preservation proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps Add coverage independent and uses it only to identify a possible bounded cleanup mapping.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents deletion of the wrong or only recovery mapping and prevents an HTTP response from being reported as the correct authorization change.
independent_technical_reasoning: Deleting a mapper entry is safe only when group resolution selects one relation and its role/member/session blast radius is known. Persisted deletion and effective authorization are distinct: cached or active sessions may retain rights, while an unrelated mapping may still grant access. Full inventory and independent identity tests are therefore required around the one write.
